name: Bombardier Thermal Defense
description: Introduces bombardier beetle chemical reaction chambers in the wrists, producing a binary chemical system that generates a superheated spray of near-boiling fluid. Two separate glands produce hydroquinone and hydrogen peroxide; when mixed in a hardened reaction chamber beneath the skin of the wrist, they produce a violently exothermic reaction that projects a spray of 100°C fluid up to 1.5 meters. The spray causes immediate, severe burns on contact. The user's wrist and palm are protected by heat-resistant skin modifications derived from Pompeii worm proteins. The reaction chambers are visible as slight bulges on the inner wrists. Discharge is controlled through specific wrist flexion patterns — accidental discharge is rare but not impossible. Each wrist holds enough chemical for 3–4 sprays before requiring 6–8 hours to recharge. The modification is loud — the discharge produces a distinctive popping hiss that announces itself.
source_organism: Brachinus crepitans (bombardier beetle), Alvinella pompejana (Pompeii worm, heat-resistant proteins)
procedure: Wrist surgery with reaction chamber implantation and heat-resistant skin modification, 3 sessions
expression_time: 6–8 weeks for chamber maturation; chemical production stable at 3 months
reversibility: Chambers surgically removable; heat-resistant skin modification persists
side_effects: Wrists feel uncomfortably warm when chemical reserves are full
Accidental discharge during extreme wrist flexion
Visible wrist bulges identify the modification
Rare: chamber seal failure causing internal chemical burns
social_perception: Feared and respected. The Hotblast is considered a more 'honest' defensive modification than poison or venom — it's loud, visible, and clearly a weapon. Some view this transparency favorably. Establishments that allow Livewire users often ban Hotblast users due to fire risk.
story_hooks: A Hotblast user's reaction chambers begin producing a different chemical compound — the binary system has been contaminated with a third substance that turns the spray into an aerosolized drug delivery system
A street fight between a Hotblast user and a Livewire user causes collateral damage that ignites a debate about biological weapons in civilian spaces
